correctness.rationale: Full unnormalized intensity/Frobenius Parseval identity reduces the nine-dimensional lifting to D_t=5uu^T+3tww^T, two copies of C_t=[[5,5],[5,5+12t]], and two levels 5. Characteristic polynomials and rank-three null generator Q=diag(3,-4,1) are directly reproduced in exact symbolic code. At t=40/81, explicit vectors v and x are true extreme eigenvectors, and their normalized Rayleigh quotients maintain exact ratio (33+sqrt(985))/4 for every positive t, giving global sharpness and uniqueness. The remaining eigenvalues at optimum lie strictly between those extremes. Rank-two trace truncation with ||Q||_F^2=26 yields the stated nonsharp-but-valid global projector inequality. No finite check is used as an infinite-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The exact optimal relative gain is a motivated, invariant design problem for two-channel Fourier/Hermite intensity sampling at the smallest possible count for complex dimension three. The unexpectedly rational unique weight 40/81 and algebraic exact condition number provide a concrete global stability-optimization law beyond the already-known qualitative identifiability. The complete singular decomposition and projector-distance certificate are directly useful for quantitative measurement design and reproducible by exact symbolic identities. The restriction to one natural frame family is explicit; no fictitious downstream theorem is asserted.
